vidURLs.title: NASA's Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 Launch
vidURLs.description:
We're bringing the holidays to the International Space Station!

NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST (1547 UTC), Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the orbiting laboratory. 

Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL spacecraft, lifting off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, will also carry fresh fruit, holiday cookies, and kits for making pizza, tacos and gingerbread houses.

The uncrewed Cygnus XL is scheduled to dock with the station on Tuesday, Dec. 1. Learn more about the timeline and the mission: https://go.nasa.gov/4eI0RBH

mission.name: CHORUS
mission.description:
CHORUS is MDA's next generation Earth observation constellation, consisting of 2 radar satellites (C-band SAR and X-band SAR), in a 53.5 degree 600 km altitude LEO, with the X-band trailing the C-band by 60 minutes. A collaborative multi-sensor constellation, CHORUS will bring together diverse and unique imagery and data sources and provide a new level of near real-time insight and innovative Earth observation services. Operating in a unique mid-inclination orbit, CHORUS will be able to image day or night, regardless of weather conditions, with daily access of up to 95% of the coverage area. From an industry-leading 700km-wide imaging swath down to sub-metre high resolution, CHORUS will provide the most extensive and unrivalled Earth observation radar imaging capacity available on the market in a single mission.

Also on board this mission are 2 satellites from ICEYE and PECCY.

Start of engine chilling
Fuel tanks are pressurized to flight levels

Launch director verifies go for launch
Start of the engine ignition sequence
First upwards movement of the rocket
Maximum dynamic pressure
Cut-off of the main engine
Separation of the second stage from the first
First start of the second engine
Separation of the payload fairing
Start of the atmospheric entry burn
End of the atmospheric entry burn
Start of the first stage landing burn
Landing of the first stage
First cut-off of the second engine
Second start of the second engine
Second cut-off of the second engine
Deployment of the Starlink stack from the rocket
